title: Traffic-shape-driven-autoscale-and-geo-fallback-prd-sketch
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a capacity autoscaling approach driven by the observed traffic shape (burstiness profile, arrival patterns) with automated geo-fallback and tenant isolation heuristics. Goal is to reduce cost while keeping latency SLOs for Dedicated customers during uneven demand and cross-region perturbations.

Context / motivation (notes to self):
- Many dedicated customers have uneven load: short microbursts (hundreds of concurrent tiny requests), long sustained increases (hours), and diurnal patterns.
- Current autoscalers are largely threshold-driven (qps or GPU util) and miss opportunity to pre-warm or gently shed based on predicted shape.
- When regional capacity is constrained, we need predictable, auditable fallback policies that respect customer isolation and compliance (some tenants cannot cross regions).

High-level proposal summary:
1) Traffic-shape classifier: lightweight online component that classifies recent traffic window into shapes: microburst, sustained-rise, plateau, noisy-churn. Output is discrete label + confidence.
2) Shape-driven action catalog: map labels -> action bundles (prewarm hotlane, throttle-low-priority, allocate-ephemeral-warm-pool, start-geo-fallback). Each bundle includes TTL, target warm-pool size, and rollback conditions.
3) Geo-fallback policy engine: when local pool headroom < buffer_threshold AND fallback-allowed for tenant, route new traffic to fallback region variant (lower-cost or lower-fidelity model) with transparent downgrade header. Routing decisions prefer same-cloud-region first, then partner regions.
4) Isolation constraints: tenants have attributes: cross_region_allowed (Y/N), priority_class, isolation_tier. These feed into action selection; high-isolation tenants get stricter non-cross-region fallbacks and prefer soft-throttles over geo-routing.
5) Autoscale backoff curves: rather than single step scale-ups, use graded curves depending on shape confidence and predicted demand horizon (e.g., quick microburst -> tiny headroom bump with fast decay; sustained-rise -> sustained allocation that ramps slower to avoid oscillation).
6) Billing and SLA signaling: optional opt-in for customers to accept geo-fallback with explicit traffic-tagging and cost offset. Logging must capture decisions for audits.

Technical details (sketch):
- Input signals: qps, 95/99 latency tail, avg tokens per request, concurrency, sequence length distribution, GPU utilization, queue depth, retry rate.
- Windowing: 30s and 5m windows for classification. Use exponential smoothing for long-term trend.
- Classifier: simple rule-based + lightweight ML model (logistic regression / small decision tree) trained on historical labeled windows. Start with rules for safety.
- Decision engine: runs every 15s, outputs candidate action bundle. Uses cooldowns per-tenant and per-pool to prevent thrash.
- Warm-pool types: hot (fully provisioned GPUs + warmed model weights), semi-warm (kernel preloads, lazy weight load), cold (no prewarm). Action bundle picks type.
- Geo-routing primitive: existing smart-router call with added constraints: allowlist, max-fallback-per-minute, degrade-model-variant flag.
- Observability: annotate traces with action-id, classifier-label, confidence, fallback-reason, target-region. Add SLO dashboards for fallback events.

Operational playbook (ops snippets):
- On sustained escalate: if predicted horizon > 10m and confidence > 0.8 -> allocate semi-warm to target headroom = 20% of recent peak or min 1 GPU. Notify customer if cross-region used.
- On microburst: if shape == microburst and tail latency > SLO -> post short hot prewarm for 60s then decay. Cap prewarms per-tenant to limit abuse.
- On geo shortage: if pool headroom < 5% and no warmers available -> try geo-fallback up to 3x QPS or until latency > fallback_latency_threshold.
- Rollback: any action reversed if tail latency returns to baseline for two consecutive windows or if error rate increases by > 2x.

Simulations and validation plan:
- Replay historical traces in sim to measure: cost delta, SLO breaches, number of fallbacks, false-positive prewarms.
- Key experiments: A/B on 20 tenants with sustained traffic, 20 tenants with microbursty traffic. Compare current autoscaler vs shape-driven.
- Success metrics: 15% reduced peak overprovisioning cost; no more than 1 additional P99 latency breach/month attributable to autoscaler decisions; <5% of prewarms that did not result in meaningful QPS.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal): rule-based classifier only, read-only decision logs. 2 weeks.
- Beta (selected customers): enable automated semi-warm actions for non-isolated tenants, geo-fallback allowed only for opt-in. 6 weeks.
- Prod ramp: expand classifier+ML refine; enable hot prewarm for top 10% tenants; full geo-fallback with billing opt-in. 3 months.

Security, compliance & tenant isolation notes:
- For tenants flagged PII/regulated, enforce cross_region_allowed = false by default. Add policy to require legal approval for opt-in.
- All fallback routing must be logged with tenant id and reason; retention policy aligned with audit logs.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Default cooldowns: 60s for microburst prewarm? 5m for semi-warm decommit? Need experimentation.
- Warm-pool sizing heuristics: should we size by requests/sec or tokens/sec? Mixed workloads complicate.
- Acceptable downgrade model variants: should default to ~90% quality model or just failover to same model in another region?
- Billing model for geo-fallback: credit or discounted rate?
- How to expose fallback transparency to customers (headers, console events, SLA credits)?

Telemetry & logs to capture (low-friction):
- classifier_label, classifier_confidence, decision_action, action_ttl, action_id, prewarm_type, target_region, prewarm_allocated_gpus, time_to_first_byte change, downstream_error_rate, tenant_cross_region_flag.

Runbook fragments (to paste into operator playbook):
- If customers report unexpected cross-region traffic: check action_id in console event stream -> classifier_label -> reason. If rollout group enabled and tenant not opted-in, immediately disable geo-fallback for tenant and trigger investigation.
- If oscillation observed: increase cooldown multiplier and require sustained-rise confidence >= 0.9 to apply semi-warm.

Next steps (short):
- Data pull: slice 6 months of traffic for 200 dedicated tenants across regions (Priya owns).
- Simple rule classifier prototype: Lucas to implement heuristics + metrics emitter (2 weeks).
- Simulation harness integration and baseline replay (Ethan & infra) (3 weeks).
- UX mock: console event surface for geo-fallback and opt-in toggle (product PM).

Notes-to-self / informal thoughts:
- Might be useful to consider cost-smoothing via short-term credits: small credit for opt-in customers when geo-fallback used.
- Keep initial ML model tiny — simpler to validate and interpret.
- Need sensible defaults for isolation: default to conservative (no cross-region) and require opt-in.

References and inspirations:
- internal: dedicated/autoscale-sim-results-2025 (confluence), SLO-handbook-dedicated, routing-fallback-spec-v2.
- external: papers on bursty traffic prediction and autoscaling heuristics.
